title: Clovis complex
summary: The Clovis complex was a widespread terminal Pleistocene archaeological technocomplex across North America, defined by distinctive fluted lanceolate stone projectile points, prismatic blades, and bone and ivory tools. Once considered the founding culture of the Americas under the long-standing Clovis-first model, revised radiocarbon dating places its lifespan within a narrow window of roughly 13,050 to 12,750 calibrated years ago, concluding abruptly alongside the extinction of North American proboscideans at the onset of the Younger Dryas.
